config.title: Build typed AST node union

intro.title: Build typed AST node union
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed union of AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) nodes to represent different elements in a simple programming language. You will learn how to use TypeScript's union types to create a flexible and type-safe structure for nodes like numbers, strings, and identifiers. The core concept involves defining multiple interfaces and combining them into a single union type, which ensures your code handles each node correctly. By the end, you'll have a foundational understanding of how to model hierarchical data with TypeScript's type system.
intro.usecase: Typed AST node unions are essential in developer tools like VS Code's IntelliSense, which needs to understand different code structures (functions, variables, classes) to provide accurate autocomplete and error checking. In build tools like Babel or TypeScript compilers, these unions enable safe transformations by distinguishing between different syntax elements during parsing and code generation. This pattern also appears in code editors' syntax highlighting engines, where each token type (keyword, string, comment) must be handled differently while maintaining type safety throughout the processing pipeline.

objectives: Construct a union type to represent different AST node categories
Implement type guards to distinguish between union members at runtime
Apply discriminated unions using literal type properties
Initialize variables with explicit union type annotations
Manipulate AST node data through type-safe operations
Configure functions that accept and return typed AST node unions
Integrate type narrowing techniques in conditional logic

steps.title: Import TypeScript type utilities
steps.instruction: At the top of the file, import the 'type' keyword from TypeScript to use for building AST node unions.
steps.hint: TypeScript's 'type' keyword is used to define type aliases and unions. You'll need it to create AST node types.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a type utility
import { type } from 'typescript';
steps.expectedOutcome: The file starts with the import statement for TypeScript's type utilities, specifically the 'type' keyword.
successCriteria: The 'type' keyword is imported from 'typescript' at the top of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing the 'type' keyword from 'typescript'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import the 'type' keyword from 'typescript' to use TypeScript's type utilities.

steps.title: Define base AST node interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'ASTNode' with a 'type' property of type string and a 'location' property of type object containing 'line' (number) and 'column' (number).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types.
steps.seedCode:
import { type } from 'typescript';

// Create the ASTNode interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named ASTNode is defined with the required typed properties.
successCriteria: ASTNode interface exists with 'type: string' and 'location: { line: number; column: number; }' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both 'type' and 'location' properties are defined with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ASTNode interface is missing or doesn't have the required properties with correct types.

steps.title: Define NumberLiteral node interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'NumberLiteral' that extends the 'ASTNode' interface and adds a 'value' property of type number.
steps.hint: Use the 'extends' keyword to inherit from ASTNode, then define a 'value' property with type 'number'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The NumberLiteral interface should be defined with the correct structure, ready to be used as part of the AST node union.
successCriteria: NumberLiteral interface exists, extends ASTNode, and includes a 'value: number' property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure NumberLiteral extends ASTNode and includes a 'value' property of type number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The NumberLiteral interface is missing or incorrect. It should extend ASTNode and have a 'value: number' property.

steps.title: Define StringLiteral node interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'StringLiteral' that extends 'ASTNode' and adds a 'value' property of type string.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword, 'extends' to inherit from ASTNode, and define a 'value' property with type 'string'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new interface 'StringLiteral' that extends ASTNode and has a 'value: string' property.
successCriteria: The StringLiteral interface exists, extends ASTNode, and includes a 'value' property of type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure StringLiteral extends ASTNode and has a 'value: string' property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StringLiteral interface is missing or incorrect. It should extend ASTNode and include a 'value: string' property.

steps.title: Define BinaryExpression node interface
steps.instruction: Create a new interface named 'BinaryExpression' that extends the 'ASTNode' interface. Add three properties: 'operator' (type string), 'left', and 'right' (both typed as 'TypedASTNode').
steps.hint: Use the 'extends' keyword to inherit from ASTNode, then define the properties with their types inside the interface body.
steps.expectedOutcome: A BinaryExpression interface that extends ASTNode and includes operator, left, and right properties with correct types.
successCriteria: BinaryExpression interface is defined, extends ASTNode, and has operator: string, left: TypedASTNode, and right: TypedASTNode properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Check that BinaryExpression extends ASTNode and includes operator (string), left, and right (both TypedASTNode).
steps.feedbackWrong: The BinaryExpression interface is missing or incorrect. Ensure it extends ASTNode and has the three required properties with correct types.

steps.title: Create the typed AST node union type
steps.instruction: Create a type alias named 'TypedASTNode' that is a union of the three node interfaces you've defined: 'NumberLiteral', 'StringLiteral', and 'BinaryExpression'.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword followed by the alias name and the union operator '|' between the interface names.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: union type for different shapes
type Shape = Circle | Square | Triangle;
steps.expectedOutcome: A union type 'TypedASTNode' is defined, combining all three node interfaces for type-safe AST traversal.
successCriteria: The 'TypedASTNode' type alias exists and is a union of 'NumberLiteral', 'StringLiteral', and 'BinaryExpression'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the 'type' keyword to create an alias, and include all three interface names separated by the union operator '|'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The union type wasn't created correctly. Review the syntax for TypeScript union types and ensure you're combining the exact interface names from previous steps.

steps.title: Create a sample AST data structure
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'sampleAST' of type 'TypedASTNode' with a sample binary expression tree. Use the BinaryExpression interface with a '+' operator, left and right nodes that are NumberLiteral nodes, and a type property.
steps.hint: Define a constant with the type annotation 'TypedASTNode'. Use a BinaryExpression object with operator: '+', left: { type: 'NumberLiteral', value: 5 }, right: { type: 'NumberLiteral', value: 3 }, and type: 'BinaryExpression'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A constant named sampleAST is created with a BinaryExpression value that demonstrates the typed AST node union in action.
successCriteria: The constant sampleAST is defined with type TypedASTNode and contains a valid BinaryExpression object with correct properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that sampleAST has the correct type annotation and all required properties for a BinaryExpression (operator, left, right, type).
steps.feedbackWrong: The sampleAST constant is missing or incorrect. Make sure to define a constant with type TypedASTNode that contains a BinaryExpression object with operator: '+', left and right NumberLiteral nodes, and the type property.

steps.title: Implement type guard for NumberLiteral
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'isNumberLiteral' that takes a 'TypedASTNode' parameter and returns a type predicate to check if the node is a NumberLiteral.
steps.hint: Define a function with a return type annotation that includes 'node is NumberLiteral' to make it a type guard.
steps.expectedOutcome: A type guard function that can be used to narrow TypedASTNode union types at runtime.
successCriteria: Function isNumberLiteral is defined with proper parameter type and returns a type predicate 'node is NumberLiteral'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function returns a boolean and has the type predicate 'node is NumberLiteral' in its return type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't match the requirements. It should take a TypedASTNode parameter and return a type predicate that checks if the node is a NumberLiteral.

steps.title: Implement evaluate function with type narrowing
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'evaluate' that takes a 'TypedASTNode' parameter and returns a number, using type narrowing to handle each node type.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses the 'type' property to narrow the union type and return appropriate values for each case.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'evaluate' is defined that takes a 'TypedASTNode' and returns a number, using type narrowing to handle each node type.
successCriteria: The 'evaluate' function is defined with a parameter of type 'TypedASTNode', returns a number, and uses type narrowing (e.g., if/switch statements) to handle 'NumberLiteral', 'StringLiteral', and 'BinaryExpression' cases.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the evaluate function, but it may be missing type narrowing for all node types or not returning numbers correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The evaluate function is not defined correctly. Make sure it takes a 'TypedASTNode' parameter, returns a number, and uses type narrowing to handle each node type.
